Much like I did its predecessor, I thoroughly enjoyed Far Cry 4. I had some gripes and niggles throughout, but nothing that would ruin the experience. I would definitely recommend this game if you enjoyed Far Cry 3 and are yearning for more good times.
For whatever reason, the story didn't particularly capture my interest. Every character felt like they were written to be total asshats. There barely was a single moment where I didn't want to punch them in their mouths. The subject matter felt kind of cliché too, on a broader scale.
The controls are still rather infuriating at times, as one button/key can be in charge of three or more game functions. I lost count of the amount of times I just swung my kukri when I attempted to do a takedown or pick up a body, usually resulting in everyone being alerted. When the controls do work as intended, it can be very satisfying taking down enemies stealthily or by pure run-and-gun methods.
I had some troubles with the game concerning the wilderness aspect, as it felt like everything was out to get you. This may have been intentional, but a sort of fatigue can set in if you're locked in a constant fight with unending beasts and soldiers. Karma events tend to occur too frequently and wild animals tend to obsess over you, including some of the prey.
The stealth aspect is still very fun and rewarding, with most situations being designed in a way that you can stealth through them. I did feel like the game had too many "forced detection" mission situations where your cover was blown for some big upcoming event despite being unseen up until that point. Also, for some reason enemies can see through certain trees. I don't know which ones and I don't know why, but they do, and it sucks.
The map editor is a nice treat for the creative types and ones who are looking for additional playable content, which is a pretty big plus.
Though I haven't played the co-op mode yet, I am very happy that Ubi actually implemented the main campaign into co-op play and I'm looking forward to playing it some day. Can't be worse than the Far Cry 3... thing.
I could make an even rantier review out of this, but I think I'll stop and let you read better ones.
UPDATE Nov 27 2017: Having played the co-op with a friend now, it's not as good as it could have been. The host gets all the progress that happens during a session, but only a few select things are saved by the co-op partner, such as weapons and skills.
Basically, to keep up with a friend, you either need to play the same activities and such twice while switching hosts, or the other person has to do it by themselves to catch up. This leads to the "guest" player always being left behind.
The co-op is still miles better than Far Cry 3's, but it is also miles worse than it could have been with just a little more effort.

A great looking game hamstrung by stupid mechanics and lack of identity different enough to Far Cry 3. The game seems to be trying to emulate a Tarantino movie (not unlike FC3), but the staged action scenes are forgettable and it doesn't really work in a sandbox shooter. They are simply forgettable compared to the situations you find yourself while exploring Kyrat. The quicktime knife fights are gone (thankfully) but there are still Boss battles that once again highlight the silliness of the forced action scenes.
Pros-
-Kyrat looks very impressive. One of the best looking environs in a game.
-Gunplay and driving vehicles is well implemeted.
-Quite challenging on Hard.
-Some decently portrayed characters and moral ambiguity.
Cons-
-Lots of locations to discover... but there's nothing there new or different. It looks copy/pasted and doesn't encourage you to go places except for the more impressive mission-relevent sites.
-The Stealth elements are not very well implemented, sometimes it seems the rules for them are arbitrary. Hiding in bushes is apparently fine but behind a tree is not.
-Similarly the gun mechanics can be shonky as well. Getting killed by snipers shooting through rocks is not uncommon.
-The wildlife.... Okay, you will be attacked very very often by pretty much anything. It gets really silly. The Eagles are the worst. I was attacked three times in thirty seconds by them. It reminded me of an even worse version of the Cliffracers in Morrowind.
-The repeated missions are all the same. There is no real variation in the different types. Worse you can barely travel down a road without one coming up. Did they not think maybe that less is more?
-The Buying system needs reworking, it is really ininspired and boring. All shops sell the same thing, money is never an issue as there is so much loot around and many of the guns are locked behiind an achievements wall... why?
-Ajay. Ajay is the main character and has no discernable personality. Ubisoft I suspect were responding to criticism of Jason Brody from Far Cry 3 as a white saviour and they went the other way... but too much. There's nothing to Ajay, his family were way more interesting and they don't even appear in it!
-Some poorly working items like the Wingsuit... I must have died twenty times because I wanted to jump downwards from one rock to another, which caused the wingsuit to deploy automatically and fly me head first into a cliff face.
In all it has a feeling of a port about it, which I'm pretty sure it wasn't. Awkward and fiddly that can be more of a chore than fun. Too much repetition and lack of variety for it's size that overshadows some fun gunplay and fast-paced action.

To all those considering buying this lil game of 1999, a fair warning: this game is part an annoyance, and part what my sharp humour and nostalgic reference-loving heart desires most. Would I recommend this game wholeheartedly? Not unless you have a computer near completely compatible with its aged requirements, like a non-Nvidia graphics card (unless its like five generations old). So let's say I recommended it most-heartedly.
The annoyance comes from the obnoxious outdated standards the game comes with, and the fact that even though there are working fixes for some issues they decrease the quality of graphics - like activating software mode to rid my screen of the flickering. The biggest pain though comes with my desktop - which is probably best fit for games around 2014, lets be honest - displaying flickering textures upon character movement, and having no conclusive fix. So, in total, this game is perfect for my laptop save the software mode activation but unplayable on any relatively up to date system.
It's a shame that no further fixes or patches are available, as this game is truly an experience worth exploring; this simple point 'n' click puzzle game holds more engaging humour and story within it than near all new games, especially AAA games. Also it's arguably more progressive in ways. Of the series, this game I feel is the most story rich and the least likely to bore you, with interesting encounters, characters, places and dialogue options. Sure, it has a one or two clichés but what game doesn't? I think this game will be one of my favourites for a long time coming, certainly worth the play.
But don't take my word for it, buy it - on sale if you're as uncertain as I was - and give it a go.

Well, plenty have done reviews over the basics of the previous Spore games, so why don't I review the extension: Galatic Adventures.
This is played in conjunction with Spore's Space Stage as "Missions". Galactic Adventures actually starts you off with a few easy Maxis-made Adventures, where you get the hang of how each adventure plays out. These can range from action-themed adventures, puzzle-solving adventures, story/quest adventures, and so on. Galactic Adventures even has an Adventure Creator, where you can make your OWN Adventures for you to play AND to share with players, worldwide, on the Sporepedia. This also adds a new list of unique buildings, vehicles, and creatures to work with (all tagged with "gaprop"), and you can create your own, too, and tag them with "gaprop" so you don't happen to get these individual creations in your Space Stage gameplay (or you don't have to).
Also, along with the adventures, each game file creates its own Captain (your creature in the Space Stage), which you can name and outfit with Captain Parts (weapons, sheilds, life/energy storage, social parts, etc), to further make each exploration (and adventure) unique.
At this point, you may spend a lot of time either downloading new adventures, or making your own; and at that point, the only real limit is your imagination.
Live long and prosper! Nanoo Nanoo!
Update: For those wondering what have I done for 2K + hours in Spore: Making playable adventures, and alpha and beta-testing them.

VA-11 Hall-A is a VN in which you'll meet a bunch of interesting characters and serve them drinks. The gameplay is very simple but does well to provide the player a way to interact and feel a part of the game. Events relating to the world and characters are for the most part explained to the player through conversation with your clients and co-workers. VA-11 Hall-A is one of those games that is quite minimal in game play, almost to the degree of a visual novel with choice selection. You play as a bartender in a high tech, low life (cyberpunk) bar where you have to mix and serve drinks to customers, buy items for your home when you finish for the day, and aim to pay your rent on time by doing your job the best you can. It's basic and, whether a difficulty setting would have been nice, it's to the point.
What makes this game completely stand out however is the sheer amount of immersive story-telling and character building that it does with the little gameplay it has. You completely get into the role of the protagonist as you play, something of a rare treat and only seen with a few, well-written visual novels. The dialogue speaks volumes to how well it works, and as a player you completely get into it. The customers you serve also have vivid and imaginative stories that expand as you go through the game. You're never bored, especially in a first playthrough.
Coupled with music that fits perfectly, an art style that fits the cyberpunk theme, great pacing of the story (you can blast through it or decide to do it in parts) and additional achievements that make it fun to re-play again (or just re-play to try different drinks and see what happens) this game is one of those hidden gems when I was craving to try something that was just slightly different from the norm. I'd recommend this at full price if you have the chance to buy it.
Great soundtrack, comfy atmosphere, funny writing, if you enjoy visual novels or story/character based games you'll probably enjoy this.

Unlike many VN or other word-based, story-propelled games you would find, this game lacks the magnetic "addiction" flavor to it. You've likely experienced it in other games or literature, the simple yet compulsive urge to read about "what happens next", the eagerness to finish the story - it is what "pulls" the readers/gamers along the story. During my experience will VA-11 Hall-A, such elsewhere-ubiquitous sense is at total absence.
Yet the game has its very own charm. You are expected to play it laid-back, and are explicitly invited to do so. The game still nonetheless captivated me, and I enjoyed every drop of it. After hours some deficiencies reveal themselves, but the game's merits still outnumber by far, and it well deserves all the honor.
In short this is a game I'd strongly recommend. Provided that you'r comfortable with the genre, you definitely should give it a chance, and most likely you'll enjoy it.

The witness is a divisive game to say the least. The people who like it, really like it. But those who go in expecting something this game is not, are almost certain to walk away disappointed. The following are just some general things about the game. I dare not call them "facts" since some things are still subjective, but I try.
Whether you will like the Witness or nor depends largely on whether you consider any of the following to be pros or cons.
1. A number of puzzles rely on color and sound, more so than you might be used to in other games. Colorblind or tone deaf players be warned.
2. Similarly, there are a handful of puzzles with brightly flashing colors which may cause discomfort.
3. The Witness is a puzzle game, far more than it is a puzzle-adventure game. It's not Myst. Solving puzzles doesn't give you a new piece of the story. It gives you more puzzles. Story is an afterthought at best.
4. The witness has decent atmospheric sound design, but is devoid of almost any background music.
5. Some sections you may do 10 or 20 puzzles in a row that are similar except for increasing complexity.
6. This game has no tutorials, no hints. Everything is determined by the scientific method. You have to experiment with puzzles to understand how they work.
7. When you solve a puzzle in the Witness, there is no fanfare, no sparkles, no gold star rating. For the most part, the only reward is unlocking the next puzzle.
8. The Witness is open-world. You can very early in the game go nearly everywhere in the island. It is also likely to throw puzzles at you in the early game that you will need to step away from and come back to much later.
9. You will always be drawing lines in this game. There are many different mechanics at work, which make for many unique puzzles, but the method of imputing the solution is always the same. Even switches and levers are line puzzles.
10. This game can be really hard, obtuse, and often frustratingly mind-bending. Sometimes, very rarely, it might also be just a little cheap.
- The bonus totally not objective section
Unpopular opinion inbound, but I think I liked this more than The Talos Principle, to which it is compared quite a lot. I like the mental process of solving puzzles, but not really the act of having to show my work, which in Talos Principle might mean 5 to 10 minutes of carrying around boxes through force fields and trying to get a laser angle just right. I already know the answer. I don't want to have to do all the grunt work as well. I want to do a new puzzle.
This game allowed me to do just that. Once a puzzle clicked, it took just a few seconds to draw it out, and move on to the next challenge. This wasn't always true. At times the pace set by the puzzles is broken by the languid pace of the world around you, which I suppose is fine, if you are taking the game at a slow pace. Near the end of the game, getting around the island between the few puzzles you might have remaining was also not that much fun anymore, and one or two puzzles were maybe just a bit too obnoxious in the way it regarded my time.
Despite this, for the most part, I loved it. It this was one of the most inventive, original and gorgeous puzzle games I had played in a long time.

TLDR; A very netflixable maze game that takes an incredible amount of evironmental awareness, fortitude and brains. Zombies need not apply.
At first glance the game gives you a really beautiful skin on a maze puzzle book you could probably buy at a gas station. What's even the point? Everything looks really nice, but why am I sitting here solving maze after maze? There really isn't anything you can do except for solve mazes, and some of them have these weird symbols that make no sense.
Then as you solve more of the mazes, and explore more of the island things start setting into place. These symbols on the mazes are a sort of syntax which tells you what you need to do to solve them. It's really quite impressive the way the game teaches you how to play it's self.  Quickly you realize that you know what you need to do on lots of puzzles, and the real challenge is a brain bending spacial math of line drawing.
The feeling you get from finally figuring out more and more mazes becomes oddly enganging. You want to learn more about the syntax so you keep solving mazes. Until you finally find one you absolutely cannot solve. All of the syntax you've learned, all of the hours you've spent, the hundreds of mazes you've solved seems like a waste. Everything in your brain is telling you to just give up. Then just after a snack break and a nap, you come back to the same puzzle and look at it under a different light.
BOOM
You solve it. You must be some kind of maze master. You have reached a zen like awareness of your space, of the island, of purpose. The endorphins of figuring out what to do next keeps you going, but it's not for the feint of heart. Although, you could always just cheat and look up the solutions if you get really stuck.
Other than gameplay, there are excellently inspiring voice acted famous quotes from really smart people scattered around the island like easter eggs. Little nuggets of litterary knowledge to fill in your gaps of sheer brain exhaustion. While there is no real 'story' the journey is something I won't forget.
I enjoy design that is unconventional and encourage games to attempt to be innovative.  The Witness succeeds in creating an interesting world that is fun to explore, solve, and learn from.
This game goes places, even if those places are the end of a line puzzle.

A neat platformer with well-made pixel art and a gimmicky but overall fun gameplay mechanic.
It basically gives you a rechargeable air dash: you can stop midair and direct the girl where you point the cursor, normally only two times before you're forced to land, but by collecting the hearts scattered around the stages you can recharge the dash meter and fly multiple times.
Levels are obviously filled with spikes, pits and chainsaws, so expect to die a lot, but the respawning process is almost instant, and the stages are usually short enough that they'll never feel too frustrating.
There are also a couple of (easy) boss fights to give a bare minimum of variety.
I used a controller because a laptop touchpad isn't great for this sort of things and I didn't have any problem, but I guess mouse and keyboard would still be a better choice for most people.
As other have pointed out, the biggest flaws are mostly a lack of diversions (same background for the whole game, and only 2 or 3 music tracks), and the extremely short lenght (took me 67 minutes, you could even beat it and refund if you're really that sort of Powerpuff Girls villain), but considering it's cheaper than McDonalds and gives you an hour of fun instead of taking away an hour of your lifespan, I guess we can forgive that.

Even if Spore wasn't as it was expected to be like at launch, it is still a great game to play.
Games like Spore don't come around often. I have never seen another game with so much freedom on what you can do inside of it. In the Cell Stage, you get to choose whether you are an omnivore, a carnivore or a herbivore. It's an extremely specific detail and it's why this game is so well made. There are many small choices like this in the game, you can become a warrior and kill everyone or trade your way up the ranks or just be a friendly race.
The Cell Stage is the first stage that you play in the game, where you must start as a small cell and work your way up to becoming a creature with legs and arms that can walk around on land. The first cruical choice in this game is deciding whether you are a carnivore, an omnivore or a herbivore. This decision can effect your abilities in the creature stage. After you have chosen, you must either eat red meat (carnivore) or green plants (herbivore) or both if you are an omnivore. The general basis of this stage is to just eat as much as you can, and eventually you will become bigger and bigger, and it roughly takes about 10 minutes to finish this stage.
The second stage in the game, The Creature Stage is one of the longest stages in the game. After finishing the cell stage, you must ally or kill other creatures until your brain becomes smart enough to create fire. This stage may take a while, and it all depends on how quickly you adapt to your surroundings and when you get certain unlocks. Overall this stage is very fun and can vary depending on what choices you make.
The Tribal Stage is the third stage in this game, and starts after you get a cutscene of your creatures learning to make fire. This stage requires you to build huts for playing music to other tribes (allying them) or building huts to equip your tribe members with weapons to destory your opposing tribes with. This stage is definitely the most stressful stage of them all, as some of the timing with the instruments are off and can purely be based on luck in some cases. Fighting with other tribes is more fun and feels more rewarding.
The second-to-last stage in this game is the Civillization Stage. In this stage, you are either preset to Religious, Economic or Millitary, depending on your previous actions in the Tribal and Creature stage. (You can manually set these if you decide to start a game at this stage.) Religious and Millitary cities have the same sort of way to gaining control of other cities, which is by attacking them. This is normally the quickest way to do the stage but can take some time if you do not decide to use the weapons provided at the near-end game on the toolbar. Economic cities, however, can propose to other cities to trade with them, which can generate you and the city you are trading with Sporebucks, and can be beneficial in the future. You gain control of the cities by buying them.
The last stage in the game and the most fun and definitely the most time consuming. This stage starts after you conquer all the cities in the Civilization Stage. The stage starts out by having you learn the basic controls for your spaceship, scanning a crashed spaceship and a destroyed civilization. The end goal of this stage is just to get to the middle of the galaxy. However, you can do many other things in this stage, such as painting planets, searching for artifacts and trading with other empires.
There is not really a story or plot to this game, as the story is mainly up to you and what you want to do. There is only a small plot point and it only features at the end of the game, once you go into the center of the galaxy.
The creation menu in this game is very unique, there are many parts that you can use to create your own buildings, spaceships, creatures and vehicles. You can even paint different colours onto your creations and make them stand out however you want, whether it is with big or small horns, or with a big mouth and small eyes, the possibilities that this game shows is endless and very enjoyable to use.
An add-on to the original game is called [Spore] Galactic Adventures, which expands your journey as an empire and lets you go down onto planets and do missions like hunting for artifacts or helping in a fight. You captain your own ship, like you do in the original game, but you can also have three crew members, just like in the creature stage, that can accompany you in your missions. The DLC also goes more indepth on what class / traits you can have, and can manually choose if you want to be a Trader, a Zealot or a Ecnomist, through the points that you earn by doing missions, you can select tools that can help you in that specific section, such as deadly weapons for the warrior and better energy storage for the scientist. Galactic Adventures is a great example of what a DLC should be. It's fun, increases the gameplay and gives you more freedom in your world.
This game is absolutely worth getting. It is so good and well-created in lots of places and gives you enough choices and decisions in the game to make it feel like it matters. The best thing about this game is definitely the space stage and the Galactic Adventures addon because it gives a fresh feel to the game and gives it a better sense of realism.

Pros:
- Fast and fluid game play. The various hero's movement, responsiveness, feels right and is a pleasure to control.
- Team composition desirable but not necessary. You do not feel obliged to pick a healer or a tank for example because your team mates all want to play dps.
- No annoying PvE mechanics such as fighting creeps and last hitting them.
- No pay to win, everything can be unlocked by playing the game. Pay not to grind.
Cons:
- Player base is small, might take a while to get a match depending on yoru region and time of day.
- A lot of disconnects by players during match making. Not sure if it is the player's fault or the game's. Regardless it make a already long match making process longer
- Match making is not very good. It is just impossible to judge a player's skill with a single rating. I might be good with one hero but terrible with another and the match making system have no way to tell which I will pick.
- Players who died too much (each death bring the opponent closer to victory), match leavers and a flaky match making system mean that even matchs is entirely dependant on luck.
- The anti cheat system can be a pain to get to run properly
Conclusion:
The list of cons might seems to outweight the list of pros. However, the game plays so well that even unbalance matches are enjoyable as long as you are not try harding to win. There are several matches that I lose 0-3, but I still enjoyed myself and got many kills. If you are the competitive type, eventually you might get tired of trying to carry the team and failing. I would say that before getting to that point this game is still well worth trying out.

VA-11 Hall-A is a VN in which you'll meet a bunch of interesting characters and serve them drinks. The gameplay is very simple but does well to provide the player a way to interact and feel a part of the game. Events relating to the world and characters are for the most part explained to the player through conversation with your clients and co-workers. The impact of the events and what they do to the characters around you as well as what they do to the main character make for a pretty unique way of storytelling which is one of reasons I was so impelled to keep playing.
The story, characters and soundtrack are amazing. The kind you'd wish to experience for the first time again.

VA-11 Hall-A is one of those games that is quite minimal in game play, almost to the degree of a visual novel with choice selection. You play as a bartender in a high tech, low life (cyberpunk) bar where you have to mix and serve drinks to customers, buy items for your home when you finish for the day, and aim to pay your rent on time by doing your job the best you can. It's basic and, whether a difficulty setting would have been nice, it's to the point.
What makes this game completely stand out however is the sheer amount of immersive story-telling and character building that it does with the little gameplay it has. You completely get into the role of the protagonist as you play, something of a rare treat and only seen with a few, well-written visual novels. The dialogue speaks volumes to how well it works, and as a player you completely get into it. The customers you serve also have vivid and imaginative stories that expand as you go through the game. You're never bored, especially in a first playthrough.
Coupled with music that fits perfectly, an art style that fits the cyberpunk theme, great pacing of the story (you can blast through it or decide to do it in parts) and additional achievements that make it fun to re-play again (or just re-play to try different drinks and see what happens) this game is one of those hidden gems when I was craving to try something that was just slightly different from the norm. I'd recommend this at full price if you have the chance to buy it.
Great soundtrack, comfy atmosphere, funny writing, if you enjoy visual novels or story/character based games you'll probably enjoy this.

Unlike many VN or other word-based, story-propelled games you would find, this game lacks the magnetic "addiction" flavor to it. You've likely experienced it in other games or literature, the simple yet compulsive urge to read about "what happens next", the eagerness to finish the story - it is what "pulls" the readers/gamers along the story. During my experience will VA-11 Hall-A, such elsewhere-ubiquitous sense is at total absence.
Yet the game has its very own charm. You are expected to play it laid-back, and are explicitly invited to do so. The game still nonetheless captivated me, and I enjoyed every drop of it. After hours some deficiencies reveal themselves, but the game's merits still outnumber by far, and it well deserves all the honor.
In short this is a game I'd strongly recommend. Provided that you'r comfortable with the genre, you definitely should give it a chance, and most likely you'll enjoy it.
Oh, and the soundtracks are great.

I give this game a thumbs up, but reluctantly so.  I think the idea behind the game is great and I would like to see more of the same.  90% of the puzzles were fantastic logic puzzles that challenges one sense of logic and critical thinking.  The artwork was also nice.
The problem is that abpout 10% of the puzzles were just stupid.  They weren't logical, or critical thinking puzzles, they were stand in the right spot puzzles.  The reflection puzzles were fine as you could use logic to figure out where to stand, but some of the other puzzles were just random.  I was only able to solve those by pure permutation and looking up the answer online.  And those puzzles weren't even challenging.  If you know which arbitrary view is the right one, then you already have the answer, no thinking required.  You just have to view the puzzle from every angle and distance until something lines up.
I want to get the answer by rational thought and logical pattern recognition, not by knowing where to arbitrarily stand.
The other problem is that this game makes some of the puzzles hard by just assaulting your senses.  If you are color blind or, like me ,have bad hearing, then you are just screwed.  The puzzles would be simple if you could understand what you are seeing/hearing, but the game goes out of it's way to make it hard to view/hear the puzzles.  And I can only assume the puzzles at end game are designed to induce seizures and discriminate against the epeleptic.
The sad part is that these crappy puzzles of arbitrary standing and sensory assaulting don't add anything to the game or make the challenge more rewarding.  It just makes it annoying, frustrating, painful, and forces one to look up the answer in order to finish.  I don't want to have to cheat to finish the game.
To the author: You have a great game here.  It is fun, rewarding, enjoyable, and worth playing.  Just get your next game play tested by people and if somebody can't handle a puzzle due to hearing/sight/seizure problems then redesign it.  Even those who don't have bad hearing will thank you for it.

Be very careful and look at the date of release before you think of buying this. It's 13 YEARS OLD!! The release date of 2001 is in very small print.
The videos above make it look like a modern game. However, these aren't in game graphics, just footage from cut scenes. When I bought this game, it was being advertised on the main Store screen as being "new!" However that is deliberately misleading and this has now become a very vocal and major issue of the way Steam is deliberately misleading it's customers (some are saying "downright rip off" on many gaming sites and gaming focused YouTube channels).
I find this very sad as Steam used to be held in high regard by myself and many, many others for it's integrity and honesty to it's customers.
As for the gameplay of WW3: Black Gold, it looks very dated now and has been left way behind by so many more modern games in the RTS genre. It just can't be compared to more modern RTS games in ANY possible way.
I bought this game and before playing it, went to visit my big time PC gaming neighbour. By coincidence, he was playing the game and was ranting how he had been "conned" by Steam and cursing the game and it's gameplay. So I sat watching him playing it for a few hours, hoping it would get better the further he got into the game. It didn't.
So when I got back home, I uninstalled it and never bothered with it again. So I haven't logged even a minute of gameplay on it on my own computer. What I saw at my friend's was enough for me.
So when I want an RTS fix, I go for Company of Heroes 1 and 2, Starcraft 2 (both of the already finished games of the intended trilogy), the Warhammer RTS games and the Paradox Grand Strategy games such as Hearts of Iron 3 TFH, Europa Universalis and Crusader Kings 2, etc.
So the lesson to be learned here is that Steam is quickly losing it's integrity and high regard in the gaming industry and so be careful to look at all the small print in the advertising for EVERY game it sells. Plus, assume "new" means the game is new to being available on Steam and not necessarily new as in made in 2014.
I really hope this isn't a downhill spiral and that Steam gets back to how it used to be which made it essential to all PC gamers.

I had shelved this game when I first got it due to being too busy and finally got back around to picking it up again. I kind of regret not playing it sooner!
The Ball has you taking on the role of an archaeologist exploring an ancient mayan-esque city buried deep underground. The only tool at your disposal is a small tool that can be used to hammer or to pull the game's main implement: the ball. You use the tool and the ball to solve the majority of the game's puzzles as well as to destroy enemies by rolling the ball over them. The game's atmosphere is pretty cozy and the music fits the visuals and I get kind of an early 00s FPS feeling from the controls (which is fine). The puzzles are very easy and you likely won't find yourself struggling for very long to move the ball along. Eventually the game throws a few "boss" like monsters at you but again these can be quickly solved through trial and error. There is also not much of a plot to the game unless you manage to find all of the secrets, each revealing a bit of the backstory to how the ball, and city, came to be. Overall I would recommend grabbing this game during a steam sale (it's not really worth it's base price of $10 IMO). Still, it can be a very comfy way to spend an evening or two.
It's okay. I honestly bought this for a Killing Floor character.

Unless you're a huge fan of first-person puzzle games like Portal and Quantum Conundrum, I can't say you should go out of your way for The Ball. The art and themes are really dry, so all you really get out of it is a bit of brain-bending.
The primary mechanic of this game is pushing and pulling a giant ball using a special ball-pushing device. The ball can be used to smash enemies, push buttons and and break obstacles. There's some story about how it's an ancient Mayan artifact or something but the story's lame enough to not be worth remembering.
The game designers did a good job of finding new gimmicks and mechanics to keep The Ball at the center of the gameplay. For being such a limited premise, it's pretty darn long. After just a couple hours in I found myself wondering, "Is there anything else they can even do with this idea?" Sure enough more ball-related puzzles keep coming. I'm impressed by their focus and ingenuity, but I must say, it gets kinda stale.

What I want to note from the beginning - this journey is reeaaally long. You play and you think: "Wow, that must be it, the final chapter", but no, there's more and more. It's an amazing, quite detailed and interesting story, and since I play the games only for a good plot, I tell you: buy it! I strongly recommend it instead of annoying romance books and superheroes-themed garbage.
The strange thing is the age of this game. There is a lot of humour here (I literally laughed out loud, and those notes in the diary...), mostly about cliches of fantasy. The main heroine is a funny sarcastic girl, but look, I thought you'd want to be sarcastic about standart plot twists now, in 2017, but...not, like, 20 years ago. There were no such amazing games, for god's sake, to annoy people with their predictability! It's almost like the scenarist is a time traveller!
I don't know though why this game feels so fresh. I've read many books, played many games and watched lots of movies, but this one... is nothing I've heard of. Yeah, sure, it has a lot of standart fantasy things like magical races, dark woods, prophecies, good and evil sides, but there are so much more sudden development twists, and it's sooooo very interesting that I couldn't get away from the game! I really wish I could erase my memory and play it once again. The atmosphere in general felt really nice, that cyberpunk here and fantasy there... There certainly could be done something to make it even better, but still the atmoshere is really high-level, the scenarist did a great job to dip us into his story.
And a female protagonist, how few of them exist! What a wonderful feeling I had while watching April go through all the troubles she had, all the adventures, and how she trolled that captain of the ship… Also, lesbian side couple. No comments, just thanks!
Aside from my delight about the story, there are gameplay, riddles, graphics, sound and one little thing more. All that keeping in mind the age of this game.
The gameplay is not very convenient, even kinda buggish? There will be some places where you'll need to go back to get a forgotten toy, to do something unobvious or the plot won't move any further and so on. There are scenes where you can't skip NPCs' slow walking (library...), where you can't properly click on something. Then again - 1999.
The riddles are fine in general. Not very difficult, most of them are quite logical... But in some places to move forward was impossible without a walkthough. Well, maybe I'm not that smart, but I just had to note it.
The graphics is, well... Okay. For a 1999 at least. Probably. You certanly will be surprised that Cortez is an old man when April will mention it... But you know, it's worth playing, despite the graphics. It's just so really good.
The sound is amazing. Very beautiful and atmospheric music will accompany your mood through the story. The voice acting is great as well, I fell in love with April the moment I heard her first sarcastic comment!
Now what really bugs me after the end is the lesson of this story. Just what did the author want to tell us? There can't be a story without a lesson, but here I can't really understand it. Help your friends? Not really. Love your family? Nah. Be ready to sacrifice yourself, to admit your destiny? I wouldn't say so. Be brave? Be kind? I don't know! That remained a mystery for me. As well as the personality of the side characters. And in the end April, her character didn't really change. Or maybe it did, but we don't exactly know it, since the game ends so abruptly. And leaves so many questions without a near-future answer...
I certainly will play the Dreamfall. And I will cherish the hope for the continuation of this beautiful story and my longest journey.

MOBAs have flooded the market. Ever since DOTA 2 and League of Legends reached the popularity of actual physical sports, there have been dozens, if not hundreds, of MOBAs looking to ape some success.
Gigantic is none one of those. It's not trying to squeeze some success out of the fruit of the MOBA tree, it's not trying to cater to the video game demographic of 18 year olds with cool tough musclemen and sexy scantily clad babes, I dare even hesitate to say it could be considered MOBA-like. Gigantic is its own beautifl, unique, and enjoyable game.
The gameplay takes a bit to get used to, but it's insanely fun and doesn't have the same problems League or DOTA have, where if you start off at a deficit, you're doomed to at least 20 minutes of boredom and deaths. There are no items, there is no direct way to get an advantage over the other team through levelling, your levels only allow you to change how your skills or traits work, and unless your team is losing super hard, to the point that your Creatures are all being solo'd and you have no presence on the map, you'll have a chance to come back after your Guardian takes damage. Hell, you might even gain an advantage if you can kill the enemies rushing your Guardian after the timer is up and the kills count.
Also, Creatures. ♥♥♥♥ turrets. Turrets are stupid, they're bland, basic, and uninteresting. Turrets in this game? A cute two-headed dog, a chubby little dragon blob, a little tree thing, and a tiny one-eyed gnome. They're interesting, cute, and change up gameplay. The Creatures took the best part of MNC/SMNC (choosing which turret type to spawn to hold areas) and expanded on it into cute baby creatures that become raid beasts if you level them up.
And, by far the best reason to play this game: The art. The art alone should be encouragement enough to at least try the game out. It's beautiful, highly stylized, all the characters are unique and distinct, there's no pandering by referencing memes or funny jokes, the characters have clear designs and backstories and their skins are alternatve versions of them from the past or present, like a skin referencing when they were younger, or part of a group they're now broken free from. You think Overwatch has interesting characters? Junkrat and Roadhog are nice, but Wu and Ramsay beat the ♥♥♥♥ out of the mad max knock-offs any day of the week. Characters in this game aren't just shallow knock-offs of other well-developed characters or universes - they ooze creativity, uniqueness, and appeal. HK-206 and Zandora aside.

Play this game. And then stop when the sadness crushes your soul. Your crew is just trying to survive and you start out raiding abandoned building for supplies. Then those buildings have been picked clean and you move on to occupied buildings. People can trade with you so bring some stuff along. You will always be on the losing end of deals and you will definitely feel it. In my own story, many of the buildings become inaccessible due to fighting and I ended up having to rob a house to make sure the crew could eat for a day. Then a hospital for meds and food to eat for another day. And then I quit. The next step would have been shanking strangers for supplies. Yes, it's just a video game and I shouldn't care about pixels dying really but this is the genius of the game.
You actually care about the crew. Sure, it's purely a stats game. This character is sad, tired, hungry, exhausted, but that member of the crew needs to stay alive, especially if they have a useful skill. Skilled scavenger has a bigger backpack. Good cook makes prepared meals cheaper. The cloud hanging over everyone's head is that you never know what you will come away with from a nightly scavenging run. Sure, the description of the scavenge site might say "lots of food" but guess what? The door at the very beginning of the building is blocked on the other side. I didn't have enough material to build a prybar or a sawblade so time to just go home. No gains at all and the crew starves for a day.
You are really watching death in slow motion. You can't stop it, only suspend it. You can have knives and guns but they won't get you through that rubble-blocked hallway. You can have a shovel but it won't help you against the thug with that AK-47.
So in the end I went from a scavenger to a blatant thief and, frankly, I wasn't able to go further. Your crew is a generally decent bunch and there were hard repercussions for stealing from a kindly old couple hiding out in their home or robbing a hospital for meds which would ensure death for some of the patients.
If you are a generally decent person this game will hit home hard. How far are you willing to go? From scavenger to thief to outright murderer? Sure, you can do all of those things without feeling anything for the crew or any other character in the game. But some of it will make you feel like a truly awful human being and that turns back around on the genius of this system.
Not politicizing this game is hard. When you watch the dismal treatment of middle-eastern refugees, the shouts of "Go back where you came from", "This War of Mine" shows you where that is. It is violent, uncertain, and makes anyone in that situation decide how far they will go to survive even if it makes you a murderer for that last can of beans. Play it and quit at the moment you can't take it anymore. You'll be glad you played but heartbroken at what you had to do to get there.

Beautiful in its visuals, interactive design, and thematic underpinnings, I've never played a more interesting game, even if I have played plenty that are more fun. The subtle, wordless tutorializing combined with meditative quotations and audio recordings  seem to me like an attempt to communicate a (somewhat lofty and pretentious, but probably not incorrect) argument from that designer that people can do so much more than they are to better themselves through study and meditation, and with the right approach, all things, even philosophy, products of creativity, and our very consciousness, can and will be eventually be *fully* understood with sufficient study and intelligence. I did indeed find myself tackling puzzles that I would have never even attempted in a game made with less craftsmanship and sense of wonder; it’s really neat to see the core interactive game bits so directly play into (what I assume) are the novelistic thematic underpinnings of the whole thing. The game's beauty and amazing capacity to just keep on delivering those wonderful "A-ha!" moments keeps you going and pushing yourself just a little bit more. *Fantastic* game.

First let me sy that I got this for a steal on sale, so can't complain too much, but
Graphics are ok (cir 2005 style), blocky 3D but effective enough
Typical RTS Gameplay, not much reasource management, just drill for Oil -> Money, focus on combat and base bulding
However, overall, this is a pretty flawed game, based on what I played at least (US campaign, then got bored).
Its tough even on normal difficulty, odds are often stacked against you, and silly restrictions (in single player campaign) such as this 1 unit must survive, and no repair capability offered, even between levels!!!?
Enemy AI is pretty simple, but effective enough... units will stay where they are, didn't see a lit of patrolling, and then they swarm as soon as you attack. Own team AI is where most of the problems are... can only set 3 basic tactics per unit/group... chase 'em, stand still, or stay within area. Even on stay within, you units often roam into areas they shouldn't and get picked off easy. Wost part is the route finding... the game relies on building many units and swarming when you outnumber the enemy... often groups of 15-20 units per group. But the pathfinding is bad. often the first 3 or 4 units head in the right direction, and the ones behind bump intoi them and then head off in another direction for an alternate, often with disasterous effects.
Base building is pretty noddy too. no sign of upgrades for most buildings, just build one to access a certain list of units and then forget it. Having to manage power was a nice touch (each gen can power two nearby buildings) which gives some tactical options of blacking-out your enemy buildings... but most of the time you'll get mashed before you get near ur enemies gens.
All in all this seems a dissapointing basic RTS cir 2000... if you want a very cheap nostagic RTS shot then grab it on sale, if not avoid, there are much better ones out there.

Just when you thought the tower defense genre has been competely explored, along comes a game that offers something fresh and new in the genre.  Defend the Cake introduces a handful a relatively easy to pick up mechanics, then layers them really well in order to  create an experience with quite a bit of depth (the later levels can be pretty challenging),  While a lot of the mechanics may seem familiar to those who have played tower defense games before (mazing, spells, resource management, etc.) here the experience is so refined that the flow never feels bogged down as in other tower defense games- you're never pulled out of the action for very long.
Add to all this a simple, charming art style and a whimsical sense of humor, and you end up with a really fun diversion in single player, with hours of potential replay value as you try various different strategies in order to improve your leaderboard score in "score attack" mode.  *thumbs up*

Defend the Cake is a step-by-step Tower defense. Before playing it, I was like, "Another BTD5 copy ugh ;-;". I was completely wrong. You start off with a basic tutorial which teaches you how to place things, start each wave and more. You place the cake on a small map wherever you want away from the ant hill. Yep basic. You have to protect yourself against enemy waves. Yep basic. Then it starts to get a bit difficult. Every level you may have a chance of unlocking a new enemy which could screw up your self-confidence. There will be more and more bugs. From worms that cannot be hit from time to time to snails that have armor to much more! This game keeps your eyes attached to the screen for a while.

Overall:

I have played a lot of tower defense games, and so far this is one of my favorites. The art style is endearing and incredibly cute, I enjoy the challenge of the strategic elements, and score attack mode is hilarious.
Also: grasshoppers with jetpacks and snails with rockets! Definitely check out this game.

I'm a fan of tower defense games and this is by far one of the cutest and most addicting I've played in a long time! Each different cake you defend is adorably unique, as are the attackers! BEWARE THE SEGWAY ANTS! Those speedy little guys can ruin a perfect run pretty quick...
After you finish each level you can play it again defending against infinite hoards of bugs for a high score, so I like that even when the story mode is done there still is quite a bit of work left to do if you want to climb the leaderboards! I would definitely recommend this game to fans of tower defense games, or really anyone looking to play something cute and fun ^_^

This is not a game you would expect to be so well designed but it's got some serious chops to its design.
Don't let the slightly cheap graphics deter you, (extremely endearing and personable graphics that they are though), this is refined and tasty little tower defense game with some elegant refining of the classic game play elements.
The build/attack cycle, the way upgrades work, the way "spells" work; these all have simpler but far better ways of working than classic tower defense. I especially like how you don't have choose between spending money on a "spell" or building a tower, which is a choice that never really  worked that well.
As well giving you all the time and infomation to make you decisions when building means in the attack phase you can be enitrely focused on when to active the "spells" and it makes a lot of difference when you use or don't use them.
So to be clear this a tower defense where you will be entirely engaged the whole time, either because it's the build phase and you have as much time as you like to plan things out, or its the night time "attack phase" where you are trying to frantically best use your spells.
(I keep saying spells, but it's temp tower upgrades that function very similiar to the classic spells in tower defense, except these are a lot more ingenius in how they work)
There's some smart as features like full money on a building cancel , and immediately showing you the path of attack that mean you never feel cheated when things go wrong.
This is some of the best tower defense I've played

When I found this game via my discovery queue, I didn't expect this game to be even half as good as what it is.
An amazing premise with an outstanding story delivered in a truly creative way. Despite never giving you prompts to choose what to say you still feel in control of the story through one of the games only gameplay elements, bartending. Not only the story but the characters bring the game to life, all of them evoke different responses from you as you get to know them. The game manages to strike a balance between light-hearted comedy and heavy emotional scenes, creating an amazing experience. The New Game+ also has a surprising amount of variance from the New Game, and with Multiple Endings, makes it very replayable.
The visuals are very appealing, striking a fantastic balance between an anime styling and pixel art. The OST is one of the best in any games I've played, sometimes I'll start the game just to listen to the music. Gameplay includes mixing drinks and buying stuff for Jill (Protagonist) to keep her focussed at work the next day, while also trying to maintain bills such as rent and electricity. It doesn't sound like much but it's all that is needed to make it very enjoyable.
I strongly recommend anyone and everyone to pick up this game, it is easily my Game of the Year for 2016.

Square Brawl is a fairly simplistic 2-4 person arena combat game that feels somewhat like a mixture of Super Smash Bros and Super Crate Box. It’s focused, fast paced and most importantly a whole lot of fun.
The meat of the game comes from the variety of weapons there are twelve different weapons of which you can pick two for any match. Each weapon offers an entirely different style of play. Weapons range from a standard gun that allows you to consistently shoot to a shield that briefly blocks incoming attacks and can damage enemies you collide with, or a bounce to get you swiftly out of (or into) trouble to a charged shot that shows the arc of fire requiring tactical placement. Whilst playing I quickly found myself favouring the rocket launcher and shotgun which meant that I only needed one good hit to wipe out my foes but left me with a tonne of downtime between each shot.
There is a decent map pool right from the start where some maps clearly favour certain types of play over others and environmental dangers such as pit and saws force you to pay attention and adds to the overall experience. The game also offers a fairly simple yet robust map editor which allows you to create and share levels. Square Brawl also offers a couple of different modes such as team play and one life bouts alongside various modifiers like double speed, health regeneration and sudden death.
Truthfully one of the main problem it suffers from the same problem that most PC co-op games do. Namely that local co-op doesn’t really work on a PC. Whilst I was able to get a few people playing together it would have been much better suited to a console and maybe with the rise of the steam machine maybe this game will become an even better purchase. I should point out that the review key for this game was provided by the developer free of charge. In terms of other complaints there really aren’t many the music is fairly uninspired and it becomes a little repetitive after a while but in all it does what it does really well.
In all Square Brawl offers a fun couple of hour and could really work as a party game. It’s a cheap and cheerful experience that appeals to a wide audience and is well worth a look.

Generally it's first to ten but you also can play in teams and do a one life run. The weapons all play rather uniquely and make your strategy different with each one.
On the plus side it's got local multiplayer, something missing alot these days. On the negative side is it doesn't have online multiplayer, something that really would make this game absolutely worth every penny. Additionally, while you can play with bots, it seems that their reload and damage rate is set differently from yours. For example, in the video above one bot had shield and could instakill with it. It wasn't until I was equipped with shield that I figured out that it dealt twice the damage I was dealing.
Regardless, at five bucks this game is a definite recommend.

What I want to note from the beginning - this journey is reeaaally long. You play and you think: "Wow, that must be it, the final chapter", but no, there's more and more. It's an amazing, quite detailed and interesting story, and since I play the games only for a good plot, I tell you: buy it! I strongly recommend it instead of annoying romance books and superheroes-themed garbage.
The strange thing is the age of this game. There is a lot of humour here (I literally laughed out loud, and those notes in the diary...), mostly about cliches of fantasy. The main heroine is a funny sarcastic girl, but look, I thought you'd want to be sarcastic about standart plot twists now, in 2017, but...not, like, 20 years ago. There were no such amazing games, for god's sake, to annoy people with their predictability! It's almost like the scenarist is a time traveller!
I don't know though why this game feels so fresh. I've read many books, played many games and watched lots of movies, but this one... is nothing I've heard of. Yeah, sure, it has a lot of standart fantasy things like magical races, dark woods, prophecies, good and evil sides, but there are so much more sudden development twists, and it's sooooo very interesting that I couldn't get away from the game! I really wish I could erase my memory and play it once again. The atmosphere in general felt really nice, that cyberpunk here and fantasy there... There certainly could be done something to make it even better, but still the atmoshere is really high-level, the scenarist did a great job to dip us into his story.
And a female protagonist, how few of them exist! What a wonderful feeling I had while watching April go through all the troubles she had, all the adventures, and how she trolled that captain of the ship… Also, lesbian side couple. No comments, just thanks!
Aside from my delight about the story, there are gameplay, riddles, graphics, sound and one little thing more. All that keeping in mind the age of this game.
The gameplay is not very convenient, even kinda buggish? There will be some places where you'll need to go back to get a forgotten toy, to do something unobvious or the plot won't move any further and so on. There are scenes where you can't skip NPCs' slow walking (library...), where you can't properly click on something. Then again - 1999.
The riddles are fine in general. Not very difficult, most of them are quite logical... But in some places to move forward was impossible without a walkthough. Well, maybe I'm not that smart, but I just had to note it.
The graphics is, well... Okay. For a 1999 at least. Probably. You certanly will be surprised that Cortez is an old man when April will mention it... But you know, it's worth playing, despite the graphics. It's just so really good.
The sound is amazing. Very beautiful and atmospheric music will accompany your mood through the story. The voice acting is great as well, I fell in love with April the moment I heard her first sarcastic comment!
Now what really bugs me after the end is the lesson of this story. Just what did the author want to tell us? There can't be a story without a lesson, but here I can't really understand it. Help your friends? Not really. Love your family? Nah. Be ready to sacrifice yourself, to admit your destiny? I wouldn't say so. Be brave? Be kind? I don't know! That remained a mystery for me. As well as the personality of the side characters. And in the end April, her character didn't really change. Or maybe it did, but we don't exactly know it, since the game ends so abruptly. And leaves so many questions without a near-future answer...
I certainly will play the Dreamfall. And I will cherish the hope for the continuation of this beautiful story and my longest journey.
UPDATE: Well, I greatly regret the decision to play Dreamfall from the bottom of my heart. That was one of the biggest mistakes in my life.

This game is a great vision with really crappy implementation, and I don't just say that because it's old. The puzzles in this game are obnoxiously nonsensical, and teh story starts off good, but becomes boring.

The story is interesting at first, but without any real events in the middle. It's like they had an idea for a good 3 hour game with the prototypical urban fantasy story: Girl is whisked away to another world, finds she has magic powers, goes on quest to retrieve magic artifact, and eventually saves the world. And honestly, that part is fairly good, (aside from the obtuse puzzles)
Except it's like they decided to make it super long by having a dozen artifacts instead of just a few, but then ran out of budget and just tore through the rest of the game. The first 3 chapters took a few hours each, and were just to get oriented to the new world. I think you're like 6 hours in, around chapter 5 when you get your first artifact. By chapter 8ish, you're like 15 hours in with maybe 3 artifacts. Now near the end, they just throw them at you. There's a chapter that's just a 3 minute cutscene where you get like 3 artifacts. It's highly uneven.
The voice acting was pretty good i thought, and the characters were likable. Interactions with the comic sidekick were certainly amusing and provided laughs without distracting or becoming annoying. The story certainly felt epic at times, although the ending was so rushed it wasn't any good.
Lots to like about this game, but the epic story at first with the overly long middle and rushed end was just frustrating for me. Add that to being a point n click with nonsensical puzzles, and it's just a pain.

So - this is a quick impressions after a few bouts in the game (using the free version at the time of review). Before I say anything else, I clicked on quick-play and was immediately put into a game. Whatever issues may have been about to cause the mass of negative reviews either didnt affect me or have been cleared up. You will need to check this for yourselves with the rest of the community. Now - the game is solid. Like - proper solid. Everything a twitch shooter needs, its here and polished. Maps are decently designed and heavily reminiscent of UT (a plus for me). The movement and shooting of weapons feels natural and theres plenty options to adjust the mouse control to just how you like it. To those who liked the old guard of the genre - this is the UT school of shooter, not the Quake one (again a plus for me). Basically - its what UT3 would have been if UT3 was more like UT2004 (and, you know, wasnt totally♥♥♥♥♥♥.
The problems here are, unfortunately, not all related to what the devs can do. Primarily - this game will live or die by its community. It needs one - its the life-blood. And twitch shooter fans will find a lot to like here. The game itself could do with a bit of a visual alteration. Looking to the inspiration - UT - the models there were visibly identifiable and bright, easy to see. A foible of the engine, however, means that its easy to blend with everything else on screen. The game does a lot to avoid this issue, but I feel they could improve it by making the characters something more than just "dude in armour" - if not for any other reason than to add some soul to the game. Weapons could also use a face lift. On paper they are fine and they are fun to use, but I didnt feel they had distinctive enough shapes when approaching them. Again, the game should look to its peers and remake the weapons to be easily identifiable by shape and colour. Make the flamer yellow and the plasmagun blue, the rocket red... make one short, one long, one bulky etc. As it is, its hard to tell, am I picking up a shotgun or a flamethrower?
Beyond that, at the minute, the community seems to be feeling the game out and the servers I tried were filled with low level players. Maybe as your conmetitive score rises, you will be matched with better, longer playing vets, but my short stay saw me pitted against other freebies (who I promptly dominated). This should change if the game gets a solid grounding. Which it should. This genre lies all buy forgotten, while having so much potential for fun gameplay. I saw this game and went to its store page.  It looked very interesting even despite the few negative reviews.  Here is my review, as of 08/17/2017, in the game's current state.
I think this concept is absolutely awesome.  Study and capture the infected, maintain your base, install security ( turrets, robots ) , play with friends, loot enemies that are military and take over their territory, even scavenge locations and take raw resources from things such as wild animals.  However, I havent found many animals besides raccoons?  I can hear bears but I havent actually seen one yet.  The graphics are also rather beautiful at times.  I had no idea you could jump in the water and when doing so, the contrast changes as well as the sound effects of submerging in water.  This is awesome.
The highlights of what I believe need immediate attention and fixing are the combat mechanics and FPS drops.  I do not have a low end computer.  I have a high end PC.  I have great FPS in this game (60+) , but at random times or more of , random locations, there is a HUUUGE FPS drop that brings me 10 fps.  Its almost as if some areas are optimized and some are not.
The mechanics of weapons when in combat with Military or Mutants, this is the main problem that I have found that has turned me sour.
- At times if you are close to any sort of object , tree, car, rock, and you decide to shoot back at an enemy who has zero problem hitting you, you shoot and a black bullet mark/hole appears in mid-air almost as if you are shooting at an invisible wall that you can not see.  I have wasted entire clips shooting enmies only to see bullet holes literally floating in mid air in a wall that I can not see.
- The Desert Eagle handgun?  It is a 1911 .45 cal side arm, that is labeled as a desert eagle.  The iron sights are literally UNEVEN.  It is almost as if your character is holding the weapon at such an angle that he wants you to question the craftsmanship of the weapon.  One side of the iron sight is higher than the other and the barrel appears to point to a North Western angle.  I do not understand this.  Also, I have a huge love for sidearms/pistols/revolvers/ call them what you will, and this killed it for me.
- The guns in general feel very clunky and just not equal or right.  I hope they tweak the weapons to feel more realistic or atleast just more functional and fluid.
I am an optimistic person and I do not bash, hate, or try to ruin any team's idea whether it be a video game, a movie script, or a play.  I will rate this a positive review only because I hope this project is unlike a large portion of other early access games and it will improve and become what it was meant to be.  Anyways, it's still afun game.  More fun with friends.  But it does need some work.
Dont waste your money.

UPD:
So I've played little more (maybe a couple of hundreds of hours more), and it's time to somewhat update this review with some new impressions and info.
First - Star Conflict is two games in one package. One game is PvP session-based tactical space shooter with huge teamwork influence and the other one is open-space based exploration game, where you just grab you ship and fly anywhere doing some missions and observing how this universe evolves from season to season. Open-space part is not very rich yet, but it grows and gets some attention from the devs with every update.
Second - some of you might think that this game is like World of Tanks with starships. Well it's not. It looks like WoT in some aspects and the hangar UI is a bit similar but the gameplay is nowhere the same. This game is ultra-fast, it requires skills and some tactical thinking. At first it's like: "Hey, here's me flying, shooting random fellas". But play just a bit more and whenever you try to just shoot random fellas with your lazors drinking some beer you'll find yourself dead most of the times. There's really a lot to master in this game. Lots of different ship classes all with unique sets of abilities. You either learn how to use them the right way, or die again and again. And you just can't fix this by throwing in some cash. You'll just get some fancy ships instantly, but they won't complete mission objectives for ya. You can spend some bucks and get some powerful weapons faster than the free players, but it's still you who shoots them.
Also as far as I know there are no cheters here, or if they are they are few and unwelcome.
Still a good game after almost 600 hrs of gameplay.

Great foundation for a beautiful arcadey space flight sim with tons of ships and satisfying scenarios.
Pros:
Intuitive and engaging controls allow for a wealth of control
Multiple effective strategical options and weapons systems for every ship
Lots of scenarios and modes
Great ship types (fast ones, invisible ones, gunships, support classes, etc)
Cons:
Pay wall for every listed pro. In some form or another, unless you pay, you will be stuck to the non competitive circuit. It isn't bad to be there really, but it takes too much effort to earn your way into upgrades for systems with the nine or ten currencies in game, most difficult to obtain.
Starting areas of main space are kind of confined and a bit empty. And the PvP and PvE servers are kind of sparse sometimes.
Pay wall is steep. A ship competitive ready can cost 20 bucks real money. It's a lot.
Advice: stick to the PvE and PvP skirmishes and enjoy the flexible gunplay and ship types. Have fun targeting bogeys. The game gets this right, and even the beginner stuff is fun to do that kind of stuff in. But if you want to test your mettle you'll have to pay. A lot. It isn't worth it unless you're willing to spend dota amounts of time in it I'd say. But taking down bogeys never gets old and flying around with this much control is liberating. It's a good way to unwind.

Square Brawl is quite a fun game. It is a simple yet fun concept which is sort of like a simplified version of Super Smash Bros. It has a good variety of weapons and maps and even an option to create your own levels! There are 4 main game modes and some conditions, I suppose that is how I'd call them, which give quite some variety to the game - things like double health, double speed, random weapons etc. You can play with bots, though the real fun comes when you play with a friend, either against him/her or with him/her against bots (I'm not sure how many players can play on 1 PC, though). However, there are some flaws. Mainly, spawn points. Sometimes the game spawns you to your, often inevitable, death. -$5

-Lots of weapon options/combinations make for different/interesting play styles
-AI that I've played is pretty decent, i've only played easy so far and it is pretty good for a beginner and learning weapons better. I'm hoping harder AI presents a good challenge as I improve.

Not bad, but could maybe be better:
-**No weapon descriptions**, some are self-explanitory, while some you have to try to find out what they do
-It has frozen on me twice over 0.7 hours of gameplay, BUT it was fine after pausing/unpausing, so it was just annoying
-Can only aim at 45degree angles, but this does make it slightly harder/you need to plan shots better in order to hit others. I could see it actually being better this way, but I havent decided for sure yet.

Yeah, it's alright. Why? Well...
The game is a large and very comical zombie road trip simulator that almost never takes itself too seriously. It's like Organ Trail if the point was to get to Canada instead of Oregon and you deal with everyone being a jerk while fighting through an endless flood of zombies. You try your best to go from the bottom of Florida to Canada while scavanging food, fuel, and weapons to survive until then. So, yeah, same old stuff.
But...
There's a lot more that seperates DRTC from the overwhelming majority of zombie survival simulations (excluding Organ Trail). For one, it's a rougue-like, which means it's so hard that you are almost never going to beat this game unless you are blessed with the luck of the Irish (or just lucky). It's also filled with an ENOURMOUS plethora of weapons, road scenarioes, and various characters, including characters from games and movies, to generic pop culture people, several animals, the infinite random generator, and any more you create yourself. There's a great selection of comedic situations and dialogue options that may at least give you a few genuine laughs. Plus, since that huge anniversary update, there's almost no bugs and plenty more stuff in general to enjoy.
However, this game may frustrate you or leave you without any smiles, depending on your opinion of these types of games. So, if you don't enjoy humor along the lines of the following scenario, then you have been warned.
"Your group has been ambushed by a group of bandits who're asking for all of your stuff or else they're gonna beat you up. How do you respond?"
A. Fred knew this was coming - "Fred, since he's paranoid, saw this a mile away. While everyone else went on ahead, he came around in the car for a double ambush! The bandits are so surprised, that they run off while you drive away."
B. Dave tells them to 'COOL IT!' - "Because telling someone to 'cool it' has never worked in the history of ever, the bandits become so enraged that they begin to beat up Dave mercilessly. Since he was already injured, Dave dies. The bandits, preoccupied, ignore the rest of your group as they drive away."
C. The Last Bodybuilder challenges them to a POSE OFF! - "The leader of the bandits, a large and burly guy, steps up. The Last Bodybuilder was hardly able to break a sweat as the bandit leader slinks off in shame and lets you guys through."
**I am not quoting this exactly, I am guessing from memory!!!**
Besides that, my final verdict is this: it's a great game that has a childish and endearing sense of humor, a well designed character roster, and many great qualities that make it quite fun if you don't try to play to win. So, yeah, it's alright, and as long as you have a similar sense of humor, then it should make for a fun few weekends' worth of good times.
7/10, It's alright.

This game is just tons of fun to play, especially with a friend. Just finished making it to Canada my first time and the feeling of accomplishment and success were very much at the forefront of my mind upon crossing the border. At times the game can be downright hilarious with moments of funny and bizarre comedy spread throughout the loose, emergent narrative. There are multiple narrative junctions in which you must make decisions and choose certain outcomes for various members of your party. Depending upon group composition this can lead to some surprising, funny or downright terrible outcomes depending on your luck.
The game is surprisingly slow at times giving the player time to plan and talk amongst friends or themselves adding an enjoyable layer of strategy and depth to what would be a mindless top down shooter otherwise. DRtC also features an intuitive and integral item scavening system in place that adds constant tension throughout as you juggle between items/weapons on you at any given moment.
You must constantly be aware of your supplies. Food, gas, meds, etc. all share the same pool for the party and must be balanced and incessantly managed, especially on the harder/ longer game modes. DRtC's art style is colorful and detailed with most character models being distinct and very stylistic, especially those that are more hidden or of the easter-egg variety. The game also boasts a rockin, chip-tune soundtrack that makes your zombie slaying that much more enjoyable.
Overall, I had more fun than I ever expected and plan to play more, hopefully with friends again. My only complaints are the lack of enemy types; different kinds of zombies/infected would have been an added bonus. Also, the lack of an online functionality is surprising as I don't always have access to a friend sitting next to me to play... at least not nowadays. Hopefully this is something the devs will add in the future perhaps.
Regardless, for 15 bucks it's worth the cash. You've got multiple hours of laughs, thrills, and  numerous means of replayability all awaiting you on your  wild trip to the Canadian border. Do yourself (and your friends) a favor and grab this one if you're on the fence about it.
